national_news.title: All India Radio Broadcasting Code and Election Coverage Guidelines
bullets: The All India Radio (AIR) Broadcasting Code prohibits criticism of friendly countries, attacks on religions, obscenity, defamation, incitement to violence, and contempt of court.
The code bars aspersions against the integrity of the President, Governors, and the Judiciary, as well as hostile criticism of any State or Central Government policies that amount to personal tirade.

The Election Commission recognizes the crucial role of electronic media and mandates strict guidelines, prohibiting the projection of only a single candidate per constituency and requiring balanced coverage of campaigns and party manifestos.

national_news.title: Overview and History of the News Services Division of All India Radio
bullets: The News Services Division (NSD) of AIR operates under the motto 'Bahujan Hitaya, Bahujan Sukhaya', delivering news 24/7 across major languages and dialects.
The first news bulletin in India was broadcast on July 23, 1927, from the Bombay Station under the Indian Broadcasting Company, which later became All India Radio on June 8, 1936.
NSD currently broadcasts 607 daily bulletins totaling 3,150 minutes across 92 languages and dialects, including foreign language transmissions like Arabic, French, and Chinese.

national_news.title: Akashwani Annual Awards Guidelines for News Services Division
bullets: The News Services Division of Akashwani (AIR) issues annual guidelines and application forms for its prestigious awards.
Notable awards include the K.L. Sharma Award for Best Correspondent, Best PTC (Piece to Camera) Award, and Best Newsreader Award.
These awards recognize professional excellence among correspondents, newsreaders, and media personnel working across AIR's regional and national news units.

national_news.title: UDISE+ 2025-26 Report Highlights Progress in School Education and NEP 2020 Implementation
bullets: The UDISE+ 2025–26 report covers 14.67 lakh schools, 1.03 crore teachers, and 24.72 crore students across India.
Maintains an overall favourable Pupil–Teacher Ratio (PTR) of 24:1, which is well within the NEP 2020 recommended benchmark of 30:1.
The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) at the Secondary stage improved to 71.7%, while the Middle stage GER stood at 89.6%.

national_news.title: India Inks Rs 1,943 Crore Deal to Lease Two MQ-9B Sea Guardian Drones for Indian Navy
bullets: The Ministry of Defence signed a contract worth approximately Rs 1,943 crore with General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc (GA-ASI).
Involves leasing two MQ-9B Sea Guardian High-Altitude Long-Endurance (HALE) Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) for the Indian Navy for 30 months.
Designed to significantly enhance the Indian Navy's Maritime Domain Awareness and provide persistent Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance coverage in the Indian Ocean Region.

national_news.title: Security Agencies Dismantle ISI-Backed Shahzad Bhatti Network in Multi-State Crackdown
bullets: Security agencies conducted coordinated multi-state operations detaining 253 people across 14 states, recording over 80 FIRs and 200+ arrests against the ISI-backed Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN).
The crackdown thwarted major subversive attacks planned ahead of Independence Day by a terror syndicate involved in targeted killings, IED, and grenade attacks.
Recoveries included IEDs, grenades with Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, pistols, and espionage equipment, highlighting the government's zero-tolerance policy towards cross-border terrorism.

national_news.title: DFS Hosts PSB Confluence 2026 to Focus on Key Banking Reforms
bullets: Organised by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, the PSB Confluence 2026 focused on seven key themes including deposit mobilisation and banking for youth.
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced that a High-powered Committee on Banking Reforms for Viksit Bharat will be formed soon.
The confluence noted that historically low Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) place Public Sector Banks in a strong position to drive the next phase of economic reforms.

national_news.title: India Ranks as World's Largest Producer of Areca Nut in 2025-26
bullets: According to the Directorate of Arecanut and Spices Development (DASD), India accounts for about 63% of total global production of areca nut (betel nut) in 2025-26.
Total areca nut production reached 15.29 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, up from 14.91 lakh tonnes in the previous year across 11.06 lakh hectares.
Karnataka is the largest producing state in India, contributing around 10 lakh tonnes, followed by states like Kerala, Assam, and Meghalaya.

national_news.title: Centre Approves Rs 1,419 Crore Estimate for Qadian-Beas Railway Line in Punjab
bullets: The Central government approved a detailed estimate of Rs 1,419.05 crore for the new 39.68 km Qadian-Beas broad gauge railway line in Punjab's Majha region.
The project features modern infrastructure including two crossing stations (Ghuman and Butala), 11 major bridges, 121 minor bridges, and 54 Road Under Bridges (RUBs).
It will incorporate 'Kavach', India's indigenous train collision avoidance system, and is executed by Northern Railway under the Socially Desirable Rail Connectivity Programme.

national_news.title: India-EU Free Trade Agreement and Challenges of EU's CBAM
bullets: India and the European Union concluded Free Trade Agreement (FTA) negotiations in January 2026.
The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entered its definitive financial phase concurrently, posing potential compliance challenges for Indian exporters.
Differences in measuring and recognising carbon costs between domestic regulations and EU's CBAM risk creating a double compliance burden for Indian industries.

bihar_news.title: Hoymiles Deploys 350 kW String Inverters in Bihar Under PM-KUSUM
bullets: Global energy solutions company Hoymiles commissioned a 7.7 MW solar power project in Gaya, Bihar, under the PM-KUSUM initiative.
The project utilizes 20 units of 350 kW HINV350HX-G2 string inverters, executed by Naw Dharam Energy as the EPC partner.
The inverter features six maximum power point trackers (MPPTs) with a maximum efficiency of 99.05% and IP66 protection.

bihar_news.title: Bihar to Resume Mining Activities After October 15
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced that mining activities in the state are expected to resume after October 15, 2026.
The state government is processing tenders for 28 mineral blocks and aims to allot over 30 blocks before the end of September.
The initiative focuses on critical and strategic minerals to boost industrial growth, revenue generation, and employment opportunities.

bihar_news.title: Ministry of Mines Organises Roadshow in Patna for 8th Tranche of Critical Mineral Blocks
bullets: The Ministry of Mines organized a roadshow in Patna for the 8th tranche of auction of critical and strategic mineral blocks along with a workshop on NMEDT.
The event was chaired by Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines Satish Chandra Dubey, alongside Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.
The 8th tranche includes 20 mineral blocks comprising 3 Mining Lease and 17 Composite Licence blocks for critical minerals like Graphite, REE, and Vanadium.

bihar_news.title: Overview of Districts and Administrative Structure in Bihar
bullets: Bihar comprises 38 districts administered under 9 administrative divisions.
West Champaran is the largest district by area (5,229 sq km), while Sheohar is the smallest.
Patna is the capital and the most populous district, and 7 districts share an international border with Nepal.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Sets Rs 5 Lakh Crore Investment Target by November with New Industrial and Education Policies
bullets: Bihar set an ambitious investment target of Rs 5 lakh crore to be achieved by November under new industrial policies and reform initiatives.
The state government announced a target to provide employment opportunities to 1 crore youths by the year 2030.
The announcements were made alongside key policy reforms and new education initiatives aimed at boosting the state's economic and industrial development.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Plans New Airports and Helipads to Boost Regional Connectivity and Tourism
bullets: Bihar government has formulated plans to construct new airports and helipads to enhance air connectivity, tourism, and investment in the state.
The initiative involves coordinating with the Union Civil Aviation Ministry and other relevant authorities for seamless implementation.
Aims to improve infrastructure accessibility across various regions of Bihar to attract investors and tourists.

bihar_news.title: Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls Led to Record Voter Turnout in Bihar Assembly Polls: CEC
bullets: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar stated that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar led to a record voter turnout in the assembly polls.
The November assembly polls registered a voter turnout of 67.25 per cent, the highest since Independence.
Around 70 lakh ineligible names were removed from the electoral rolls during the three-month mammoth revision exercise.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Government to Build 100 Modern Bus Stands to Strengthen Urban Infrastructure
bullets: Bihar government announced plans to construct over 100 modern, state-of-the-art bus stands to improve road transport connectivity.
The announcement was made during the unveiling of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's statue in Jamui district.
Aims to accelerate industrial development and strengthen urban infrastructure, alongside healthcare upgrades across 36 district hospitals.

bihar_news.title: Railway Ministry Approves Sherghati-Kajree Broad Gauge Rail Link Connecting Bihar and Jharkhand
bullets: Railway Ministry issued a sanction memorandum for the 107.89-km broad gauge railway line connecting Sherghati (Gaya, Bihar) and Kajree (Palamu, Jharkhand).
The estimated cost of the project is ₹2,627.29 crore, executed by the East Central Railway.
The project is expected to reduce travel distance by about 70 km and boost trade, business, and employment opportunities in the region.

bihar_news.title: Bihar CM Warns Government Doctors Against Unnecessary Patient Referrals
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary issued a strict warning to government doctors against unnecessary patient referrals during a public event in Jamui.
The state government is equipping district and sub-divisional hospitals to perform 36 types of surgeries to ensure quality treatment locally.
The event also marked the unveiling of a statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in Jhajha, with several state ministers in attendance.
